task: Replace the runtime sidewalk solver with baked, committed sidewalk polygon data generated once from the hand-authored road network
context: Matsubara Town's road network is hand-authored constant data: ROAD_SEGMENTS in src/config/town.js is a literal array of 41 segments, and it never changes at runtime. The sidewalk geometry is therefore a pure function of a constant, but createRoads() currently re-derives it on every load with an O(edges^2) clearance search that retreats each walk from its junctions. That solver leaves the pavement broken at every junction: 155 of 164 walk ends stop short, 334.8 units of pavement missing, worst gap 13.75. An attempt to close the corners with radially-sampled ribbons failed three ways (chords cutting across a carriageway, per-quad boxes z-fighting into visible combs, 9 of 82 corners never emitted) and has been reverted. The decision is to stop solving a fixed layout at runtime and bake the geometry instead.
requirements: Add scripts/bake-sidewalks.mjs which imports ROAD_SEGMENTS and ROAD_WIDTH from src/config/town.js, builds the road graph the same way src/world/graph.js does, computes the complete sidewalk and kerb geometry, and writes src/config/sidewalks.js. Add an npm script `bake:sidewalks` for it.

Compute each corner ANALYTICALLY as a miter joint between two offset strips, not by sampling. A road's kerb line is its centreline offset by width/2; its outer line is offset by width/2 + sidewalk width. For a pair of angularly adjacent edges at a node, the corner fill is the polygon bounded by both kerb lines and both outer lines; each straight strip runs up to the neighbouring road's kerb line. Bevel the outer vertex when an acute angle makes the miter spike longer than 3x the sidewalk width.

Every emitted polygon must be clear of EVERY carriageway, including roads not incident to the node it sits at - clip against those too. A stub edge swallowed by its junctions must still end up with continuous pavement across it.

src/config/sidewalks.js must be plain committed data a person can read and hand-edit, in exactly this frozen format: `export const SIDEWALK_SOURCE_HASH = '<hex>';` (a hash over ROAD_SEGMENTS and ROAD_WIDTH), `export const WALK_POLYGONS = [ [[x,z],[x,z],...], ... ];` and `export const KERB_POLYGONS = [ [[x,z],...], ... ];`. Coordinates rounded to 3 decimals, one polygon per line, so the file diffs cleanly in git.

createRoads() in src/world/roads.js must draw the sidewalks and kerbs from that committed data only. Delete the runtime clearance search, the retreat loop and the per-edge walk/kerb slab emission it feeds. Carriageways, the junction asphalt discs, zebra crossings, centre lines and createLotSidewalk() stay exactly as they are.

Build each polygon as ONE extruded prism - a single top face at the existing WALK_TOP (kerbs at WALK_TOP + 0.03) with vertical faces only around its outer perimeter. No internal faces between neighbouring pieces: coincident coplanar faces are what produced the z-fighting combs last time.

Add a staleness guard: at load, hash ROAD_SEGMENTS and ROAD_WIDTH the same way the bake script does and compare against SIDEWALK_SOURCE_HASH. On mismatch, log a clear console error naming the `npm run bake:sidewalks` fix. It must fail loudly rather than silently drawing stale pavement.
Update .ai/audit-sidewalk-gaps.mjs to audit the baked result: it must report 0 unpaved corners of 82, 0 carriageway intrusions, and 0 hash staleness, and exit non-zero if any of those fail.
constraints: Do not touch pedestrian routing (systems/pedestrians.js), the road graph (world/graph.js), vehicles, landmarks, or lot code. src/config/town.js is READ-ONLY - do not edit the road network to make the geometry easier.
No pavement may lie on a carriageway at any point along a polygon edge, not merely at its vertices. This is the regression the old retreat rule existed to prevent.
The painted zebra crossings on junction approaches (at maxW/2 + 1.8 from the node) must stay visible on asphalt - pavement must not cover them.

Draw calls must not increase: everything still merges via mergeInto() into the existing 'sidewalks' and 'kerbs' meshes. No per-frame work is added - the runtime only reads data and builds static geometry once.
Keep the total triangle count for sidewalks and kerbs in the same order as before; an analytic miter should need far fewer triangles than the reverted sampled version.
Do not inline code into shell commands (no `node -e`). Use the declared npm scripts.

Record the decision in DESIGN_DECISIONS.md: baked committed geometry replacing a runtime solver for a fixed hand-authored layout, why (the solver kept producing junction defects on a layout that never changes), and the staleness guard that makes hard-coded data safe.
notes: The audit needs a preview server: `npm run build`, then `npx vite preview --port 4177 --strictPort` in the background, then `npm run audit:sidewalks`. It drives the live game with Playwright against Chrome at 'C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe' and reads window.game.world.graph under ?dev=1. Current audit baseline on the reverted code: unpavedCornerCount 9 of 82 was the best the sampled attempt reached; the straight-run metrics gapCount 155 / totalMissingMetres 334.8 describe the retreat and are expected to become meaningless once walks run to the kerb lines - replace them with the corner/intrusion/staleness checks rather than preserving them. Also re-run `node .ai/verify-pedestrian-flow.mjs dist` and confirm it still passes. Capture a fresh top-down to qa-evidence/sidewalk-baked-topdown.png: corners must read as smooth flat pavement with no ridges, combs or stripes.
